insights.topic: Verified purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's cryptographically verified receipts confirm a purchase occurred — not inferred from browsing behavior. At ~$0.10 per verified receipt, the cost-per-confirmed-transaction is orders of magnitude below the $5+ CPM brands pay for probabilistic audience inference.

Grocery-supermarkets leads by receipt volume (1,400 receipts, 14-day) while retail-department-stores leads by GMV ($35,379 vs. $30,650) despite 582 fewer receipts — a measurable average-ticket gap that separates category audiences by spend behavior, not just purchase frequency.

insights.topic: Brand concentration at the top of the receipt stack
insights.insight: Walmart (333 receipts), Costco (149), and Kroger (145) account for a disproportionate share of 14-day verified volume; Safeway and Publix trail at 127–130. For CPG and FMCG brands, this confirms the protocol's audience skews toward mainstream mass and club-channel shoppers, not specialty retail.

7-Eleven and Circle K both crossed the brand-visibility threshold within the past week, anchoring a gas-convenience category with 621 receipts and $24,717 in 14-day GMV. This channel captures impulse and top-off purchase occasions that are notoriously difficult to attribute in traditional media buys.

insights.topic: Settlement latency is a real constraint
insights.insight: 809 confirmed payouts have not moved in 45+ consecutive snapshots spanning Oct 28–Nov 02 — the longest zero-payout run on record. Brands evaluating this protocol for real-time incentive or loyalty applications should model settlement as episodic and delayed, not instant.

insights.topic: Geographic expansion is accelerating but uneven
insights.insight: Three new CBSA metro cells appeared in under five days after a stable coverage period, bringing the visible surface to 18 metro areas across 30 category/metro cells. Coverage growth may reflect delayed signal aggregation rather than confirmed new market entry — metro-level targeting claims should be validated against snapshot timing before activation.
